observations.text: SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations and with the formation Leader with the IP directing the sequence of calls, which is the desired standard for this Training Section. Confirmation of the Leader's directions was passed twice only after the IP indicated the required wording. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent read-back of formation directions is expected to improve.

SP, with only verbal prompting from the IP on the timing of the frequency change, maintained R/T contact with the ground stations and with the formation Leader and passed the formal position reports without the IP having to transmit any of them. Every direction from the Leader was confirmed, with slight delay on the first two calls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations, the other A/C and the formation Leader throughout the mission, confirming every given information and direction. Two transmissions overlapped the Leader's calls and were repeated on SP's own initiative, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with ground stations and formation members throughout the mission with accurate and standard phraseology, and passed the formal position reports at the briefed points. Every information and direction from the Leader was confirmed promptly, and the Leader's radio comm with the ground stations was monitored continuously. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with ground stations, other A/C and formation members with impeccable and standardized phraseology, passing all formal position reports at the briefed points with no repeat request from any station. Acting as Leader, SP provided accurate information to the Wingman and reminded the functional A/C checks and the fuel check at the planned points. As Wingman, SP monitored the Leader's radio comm and interfered only where demanded for flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized radio setup flow, did not select the briefed inter-flight frequency before departure and did not maintain R/T contact with the formation Leader after the change, with the result that the IP had to set the frequency and transmit the join-up call. Radio management during the departure segment requires further study.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the SP flying and transmitting at the same time, did not confirm the directions given by the formation Leader and did not pass the formal position report to the ground station, with the result that the IP directed the calls and transmitted part of them. R/T contact during the recovery segment was maintained only with IP assistance.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations and the formation members and completed the required calls with the IP's verbal prompts, as expected for this Training Section. Two directions from the Leader were confirmed only after the IP indicated the correct read-back, and the omissions were recognized with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness in confirming the Leader's directions is expected to improve.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations and with the formation Leader without verbal prompting from the IP, confirming every given direction. One position report was passed in non-standard wording and was restated correctly on SP's own initiative on the next transmission, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with ground stations and formation members throughout the mission, using standard phraseology and passing the formal position reports accurately and at the briefed points. Every information and direction from the Leader was confirmed without delay and without any prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations, the other A/C and the formation members throughout the mission with impeccable and standardized phraseology and with no repeat request from any station. As Wingman, SP monitored the Leader's radio comm continuously and interfered once, where demanded for flight safety, with a timely and correctly worded call. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the briefed frequency plan, did not maintain R/T contact with the ground station after the area change and did not pass the formal position report, with the result that the IP had to select the correct frequency and transmit the report. The formation Leader repeated two directions before they were acknowledged.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in requesting a repeat of the instruction that was not understood, did not confirm the information given by the formation Leader, with the result that the IP had to state the direction and transmit the confirmation on SP's behalf. The exchange was completed only under IP direction.

SP, due to a radio scan that was interrupted during the join-up, did not confirm two directions given by the formation Leader and omitted one formal position report to the ground station, with the result that both were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to non-standard phraseology that left the intention ambiguous to the controller, did not pass the formal position report in the prescribed format, with the result that the ground station requested a repeat and the correct wording was transmitted only after the IP's verbal prompt. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations and with the formation members within the desired standards, confirming the given directions without IP intervention. However, two transmissions were made simultaneously with the Leader's calls and were repeated on SP's own initiative. Marginal performance for the Training Section - discipline in listening out before transmitting is expected to improve.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations, the other A/C and the formation members throughout the mission, passing every formal position report accurately and at the briefed points. Every information and direction from the Leader was confirmed promptly and with standard phraseology, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained R/T contact with ground stations and formation members with impeccable and standardized phraseology throughout the mission, with no repeat request from any station and no IP intervention. Acting as Leader, SP provided accurate information to the Wingman and reminded the functional A/C checks and the fuel check at the planned points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized frequency change technique, did not maintain R/T contact with the ground station during the recovery and missed two calls addressed to the formation, with the result that the IP had to reset the radio and transmit the answering call. The formal position report at the initial point was passed by the IP.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not monitor the Leader's radio comm with the ground station and did not confirm two directions addressed to the formation, with the result that the IP had to answer for the A/C and direct the subsequent calls. Radio monitoring within the formation was maintained only with IP assistance.

SP, due to a read-back technique that repeated only part of each instruction, did not confirm every given information and direction from the formation Leader, with the result that two directions were correctly acknowledged only after the IP's verbal prompts. The omissions were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to reluctance to challenge a decision perceived as the Leader's prerogative, did not interfere on the radio when the Leader's read-back of the recovery clearance differed from the clearance issued by the ground station, with the result that the correction was transmitted only after the IP's verbal prompt. The discrepancy was recognized with delay.

SP, due to a slightly delayed selection of the briefed frequency, missed the first call from the formation Leader after the change, with the result of a short break in R/T contact that SP recognized and restored with a timely check-in call, without IP intervention. All subsequent directions were confirmed correctly and the formal position reports were passed at the briefed points.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased during the rejoin, passed the formal position report to the ground station later than the briefed point, with the result of a minor deviation in reporting timing that was recognized and corrected on the next transmission without IP intervention. R/T contact with the formation members was maintained throughout.

SP maintained R/T contact with the ground stations, the other A/C and the formation members throughout the mission and confirmed every given direction from the Leader without IP intervention. However, two formal position reports were passed with hesitation and non-standard wording before being restated correctly. Marginal performance for the Training Section - fluency and standardization of phraseology are expected to improve.

SP maintained R/T contact with ground stations, other A/C and formation members throughout the mission with impeccable and standardized phraseology, passing every formal position report accurately and at the briefed points with no repeat request from any station. As Leader, SP provided accurate information to the Wingman and reminded the functional A/C checks and the fuel check on time; as Wingman, SP monitored the Leader's radio comm continuously and interfered only where demanded for flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.
